messages:
Dmitri: ran a focused nsys on a 4-GPU Dedicated pod, repro for the odd tail latency we saw this morning. attaching short summary and timeline :eyes:
Dmitri: nsys slice shows repeated small kernels on GPU1 while GPU0 is busy — looks like queue-stealing in the wrapper/scheduler boundary
Dmitri: command I used:
```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx -o out/trace_2076 --sample=none 
  --capture-range=nvtx -t 5s python perf/invoke_driver.py --model trt-llm-slim --batch 1 --seq 384
```
Dmitri: key snippet from the timeline (cropped):
```
[GPU0] conv_fp16 (long compute) -> kernel T=9.3ms
[GPU1] wrapper_postprocess (short) -> memcpy+small kernels repeated 3x T=0.9ms each
[GPU1] scheduler_dispatch (spin) -> waiting 4.2ms
```
Jena: can you paste the nvtx labels around the wrapper boundary? curious if the engine call returns earlier or the wrapper loops
Dmitri: nvtx shows: `engine.invoke.start` / `engine.invoke.end` bracketed, but between end and next invoke.start we have `wrapper.copy_kv` and `wrapper.sched_yield` NVTX ranges
Maria: hunch: kernel selection fallback may be picking a non-optimal cuBLAS/cublasLt path which fragments SM occupancy and forces micro-copying in wrapper. did you capture per-kernel occupancy/SM utilization?
Dmitri: yes — attached in the nsys report: occupancy for the small kernels is ~12-18% vs ~78% for the big conv on GPU0. perf numbers: p50 ~ 24ms, p95 ~ 174ms (spikes correlated with those micro-kernels)
perfbot: metric alert: trt-llm-service.p95 increased +42% in the last 2h (correlates with 07:10 deploy) :rotating_light:
Sam: @Dmitri can you try setting TRT_FORCE_KERNEL_SELECTION=prefer_high_occupancy and re-run? also try disabling the wrapper micro-batch coalesce to see if it reduces the handoff churn
Dmitri: will run two quick experiments: (1) env var set, (2) wrapper coalesce off via `WRAPPER_COALESCE=false`
ci-bot: artifacts uploaded: nvtx + nsys zip -> https://ci.redwood/artefacts/2076543210/traces.zip
Jena: if (1) reduces the small kernels but increases single-kernel latency, we might need a scheduling heuristic: prefer fewer high-occupancy kernels up to X tokens, else prefer low-latency kernels. worth a micro-sweep
Maria: also check KV cache warmup: looks like wrapper is doing per-request KV syncs when fallback kernel changes cache layout. add `--kv-warmup 2` to the driver for the next run
Dmitri: running experiments now, I'll post concise diffs. owner: Dmitri to validate kernel-affinity + coalesce sweep, follow-up in ~1.5h :thumbsup:
